revisions.title: Stock charges and named accusers
revisions.body: The slanderers fill the jurors’ ears with stock charges about Socrates. Meletus, Anytus, and Lycon attack him in connection with poets, artisans and public men, and orators.

revisions.title: The better lot known only to God
revisions.body: Socrates says that no evil comes to a good man. He asks the jurors to rebuke his sons if they value money over virtue or think themselves important. He says that he goes to die and they go to live, and that only God knows which lot is better.
Socrates says he is not wise. He questions the oracle, investigates a public man reputed wise, finds that the man seems wise to himself but is not, and tries to show this.
